Class ImuMountCheck

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.localization.ImuMountCheck
All Implemented Interfaces:
Check
public final class ImuMountCheck extends Object implements Check
Checks, from logged inputs, that the gyros are mounted the way the code is told, against the drivetrain's own wheel motion. Each check waits for enough evidence, then holds a verdict. As a pre-match Check, a reversed yaw sense fails, any other wrong mount warns, and a robot that has not driven enough since boot to judge anything is skipped.
  • Pigeon level: at rest, mount-corrected pitch and roll near 0.
  • Pigeon forward: while the wheels accelerate hard, the Pigeon's X/Y acceleration points the same way. A Pigeon turned on its mount reads the turn here.
  • Yaw sense, both gyros: the heading turns the way the wheels turn the robot.
  • Onboard IMU orientation: at rest, gravity on the axis its mount setting implies. WPILib applies the mount orientation to yaw only, so the raw accelerometer shows how SystemCore really sits.

Evidence counts only when the gyro and the wheels move together. Wheels spinning on a cart, pushing a wall, or a robot carried by hand give none, so a gyro that simply does not follow the wheels is never called wrong. Rests count only shortly after such driving, so the robot is on the floor. A check reads wrong only on clear contrary evidence: a reversed yaw, a consistent acceleration direction far from the wheels', a pitch, roll or gravity axis a mount error away.

Each rest is judged on its own, and a rest-based check reads wrong only when every rest does. A mount error tilts every rest alike, while a robot tipped on a bump or lifted with its wheels still tilts only that rest.

Call update(ImuMountCheck.Inputs) every loop, enabled or not: most evidence comes from driving.
